_readme: Curated Ghanaian civic knowledge base for RumorShield. Each record is a known, source-verified fact or debunked claim. Incoming user claims are matched against these records by InternalReasoningEngine (rule-based extraction + templated explanation) and ClaimMatchingService (deterministic verdict logic) — no LLM or external API is involved anywhere in the pipeline.

records.subject: Ghana Card annual renewal fee (district office)
records.verifiedFact: Annual Ghana Card renewal at NIA district offices costs GHS 150, effective 2 February 2026.
relatedFacts: First-time registration (25+ years) at district offices: GHS 30
Card replacement at district offices: GHS 200
Foreign nationals: renewal costs the cedi equivalent of USD 78/year
records.notes: Legal basis: Fees and Charges (Miscellaneous Provisions)(Amendment) Regulations 2025, L.I. 2512. In August 2026 the NIA publicly rebutted circulating reports as 'misleading', confirming the fee schedule was parliamentary-approved, not unilaterally imposed — good real example of an institution responding to misinformation.

records.subject: Ghana Card fees at the 24-Hour Prestige Registration Centre (Labone)
records.verifiedFact: At the Prestige Centre, first-time registration and renewal each cost GHS 610; replacement costs GHS 720. This is a separate, optional premium service — not the standard fee.
records.notes: Useful for a claim like 'Ghana Card now costs GHS 610' — true only for the optional Prestige Centre, not district offices. Good demo of nuance beyond true/false.

records.subject: Free NHIS registration/renewal promotion
records.verifiedFact: NHIS ran a free registration and renewal promo (normal fees and 30-day waiting period waived) from 15 April to 31 May 2026, under the Mahama Care primary healthcare initiative.
records.notes: PERFECT for the OUTDATED status demo: a claim that 'NHIS registration is free right now' was TRUE during the promo window but is FALSE as of any date after 31 May 2026 (i.e. false today, 14 Sept 2026). Normal premium outside promo: GHS 7-50/year depending on source, varies by district — flag as approximate, not a hard verified figure.

records.subject: Standard 32-page passport application fee
records.verifiedFact: The standard 32-page Ghanaian passport costs GHS 350, down from GHS 500, effective 13 November 2025 following Cabinet and Parliamentary approval.
records.sourceName: Ministry of Foreign Affairs / ghanacitizenship.com reform summary
records.notes: IMPORTANT: other sources (a Ghana News Page article dated April 2026, and Wikipedia) list GHS 500 or GHS 640 for the same passport — these are stale/aggregator figures that never updated after the Nov 2025 cut. This is a genuinely useful CONTRADICTED demo case: a user claim of 'passport costs GHS 500' would be flagged against the more authoritative, more recent MFA-sourced figure of GHS 350.

records.subject: 24-hour expedited passport processing fee
records.verifiedFact: A 24-hour expedited passport application service costs GHS 2,000, introduced as part of the passport reforms programme.

records.subject: Claim: President Mahama is giving out a GHS 1,500 'development cash grant'
records.verifiedFact: This is a confirmed SCAM, not a real government programme. It uses a fake website with official state symbols, asks users to share the link to WhatsApp groups to 'unlock' the payment, and never pays out — a classic engagement-harvesting hoax.
records.notes: Excellent CONTRADICTED demo claim — real hoax, real fact-check, very close in style to genuine viral WhatsApp scams your users will encounter.

records.subject: Claim: GoldBod lost GHS 200 million to a former security guard
records.verifiedFact: False. GoldBod publicly clarified via its official website and X account that the claim was untrue. It originated as a viral flyer on Facebook and X.

records.subject: Claim: President Mahama closed down all US military bases in Ghana
records.notes: Publish date approximate — archive listing did not give exact date; verify before using in final demo if precision matters.

records.subject: Police clearance certificate fee (ordinary vetting, resident)
records.verifiedFact: An ordinary police clearance certificate (resident) costs GHS 150, payable at Nima Divisional Police Headquarters, Accra, plus two passport-size pictures with red background.
relatedFacts: Employment vetting / fingerprint request (CID Form 59): GHS 100
records.sourceName: Ghana Police Service — official Paid Services fee schedule
records.notes: Published by the GPS Public Affairs Directorate explicitly 'to reduce the perception of corruption' — good citable framing for the demo. Exact publish date not shown on the page; treat as current as of research date (Sept 2026).

records.subject: Claim: guaranteed Ghana Police Service recruitment slots available for a fee
records.verifiedFact: Recurring scam pattern, not a real recruitment channel. Criminal syndicates — sometimes involving rogue officials — have repeatedly advertised fake enlistment slots in the Ghana Police Service in exchange for payment. A 2014 case implicated a senior police officer (DCOP Patrick Timbilla) in exactly this scheme. The Police Service does not sell recruitment slots; official recruitment goes through its own published, fee-free process.
records.sourceName: Ghana Police Service recruitment-scam pattern (background via Wikipedia, citing GhanaWeb/MyJoyOnline reporting)
records.notes: This is a recurring pattern rather than one dated claim — treat any 'pay for a guaranteed police job' message as matching this record regardless of which year it resurfaces in.
